subject.declared_domain: The directedness of CloudEdge in the kuzu_nessie_db projection -- the property D2 relies on when it declares 'direction: NATIVE -- CloudEdge is directed (a -> b)' and defines a path as the transitive closure over produces/consumes/FLOWS_TO. This card covers direction AS A PROPERTY OF THE EDGE STORE: where it comes from, whether it is real, what it spans and how it fails. It does NOT card the edge types themselves (W2-kwjy) or the D2 rail (wave 1, SC-f-*).

methodology.how: ⛔ DIRECTION IS NOT A FIELD ON AN EDGE -- IT IS A PROPERTY OF THE STORAGE MODEL, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE SUBSTANCE OF THIS SUBJECT. CloudEdge is a Kuzu REL table (CALL show_tables() returns type=REL), and Kuzu REL tables are directed by construction: every edge is stored as an ordered (source, destination) pair. Nothing in the edge's own property set carries a direction flag -- table_info('CloudEdge') returns exactly four properties (edge_type, layer, snapshot_ts, props) and none of them is directional. So direction COMPOSES the storage engine's relationship model rather than being invented by the estate, and the estate's contribution is the CHOICE to model produces/consumes as directed edges instead of as a symmetric relation carrying a role field. It INVENTS the closure semantics D2 rests on -- that walking those directed edges transitively IS a path.

composes.note: the Kuzu relationship-table model; directedness is inherited from it, not implemented per-edge
the single REL table carrying every edge in the projection

invents.note: the declaration that a transitive walk over directed produces/consumes/FLOWS_TO edges constitutes a path -- D2's foundational move
modelling produce and consume as opposite-direction edges rather than one relation with a role property

declared_opinions: DIRECTED-NOT-ROLED: produce and consume are modelled as direction rather than as a role field on a symmetric relation. A consumer cannot ask 'what relation holds between a and b' without also choosing which way to look.

ONE REL TABLE FOR EVERYTHING: all 53 edge types share a single CloudEdge table and are discriminated by an edge_type STRING property rather than by separate typed relations. Directedness is therefore uniform across every semantic edge type, whether or not that type is naturally asymmetric.
CLOSURE IS A PATH: that a transitive walk over directed edges constitutes a meaningful path is a modelling choice inherited by every D2 derivation, including provenance and blast-radius.
methodology.evidence: Storage model measured directly at the pinned vintage: comp-kuzu 'CALL show_tables() RETURN *' returns exactly two tables -- CloudEdge (type REL) and CloudNode (type NODE). Property set measured with 'CALL table_info(''CloudEdge'') RETURN *' -> four properties (edge_type STRING, layer STRING, snapshot_ts INT64, props STRING); NO directional property exists, which is the positive evidence that direction is structural rather than declared per-edge. Per the standing currency rule, absence of a currency measurement is not evidence of currency, so 'unknown' is the honest value rather than a guess in either direction.

It is a schema property that exists for as long as CloudEdge is a REL table, and it is re-established on every rebuild of the projection rather than maintained. The projection's own build is what carries a cadence; direction inherits it and cannot drift independently.

key.identity_space: The ordered pair (source CloudNode id, destination CloudNode id) together with edge_type. Direction is what makes the pair ORDERED rather than a set, so it is constitutive of edge identity rather than an attribute of it.
key.key_expression: The ORDERED TRIPLE projected straight off the edge row: (source CloudNode.node_id, CloudEdge.edge_type, destination CloudNode.node_id) -- in the graph's own dialect `MATCH (a:CloudNode)-[e:CloudEdge]->(b:CloudNode) RETURN a.node_id, e.edge_type, b.node_id`. Three column reads; NO serialization grammar is given because none is declared anywhere in the estate, and inventing a delimiter here would invent a key space rather than describe one. The tuple is ORDERED, not a set: exchanging the first and third members yields a DIFFERENT key, which is precisely what makes direction constitutive of edge identity rather than an attribute of it.

failure_mode.returns_on_failure: A CLEAN, WELL-FORMED ZERO. Querying a directed edge in the wrong orientation returns an empty result set with no error, no warning and no hint that the reverse orientation would have matched. 'These nodes are unrelated' and 'you asked in the wrong direction' are byte-identical answers.
silent_degrade_paths: a reversed query returns 0 rather than an error -- measured below at exactly 0 against a true value of 280
a consumer walking the closure in the wrong direction gets a well-formed but empty provenance or blast-radius answer, and emptiness is a legal result for both

because all 53 edge types share one REL table, an edge type that is naturally symmetric is still stored asymmetrically, so a consumer must know per-type which orientation is meaningful and nothing in the schema tells them
failure_mode.evidence: ⛔ EXERCISED AS A CONTROL PAIR REACHABLE FROM DIFFERENT TRUTHS, which is what makes this a measurement rather than a restatement of the storage model. ARM 1, the declared orientation: MATCH (a)-[e:CloudEdge]->(b) WHERE e.edge_type='WRITES' AND a.node_type='LAMBDA' AND b.node_type='S3_BUCKET' -> 280. ARM 2, THE SAME EDGE TYPE REVERSED: a.node_type='S3_BUCKET' AND b.node_type='LAMBDA' -> 0, returned as a normal successful result set with no error and no marker. The pair proves two things at once: direction is REAL (a symmetric store would have returned 280 both ways) and its failure is SILENT (the wrong orientation returns a clean zero). It is also semantically sound in this instance -- a bucket does not write a lambda -- so the 0 is a true negative here, which is precisely why it is indistinguishable from the false one a consumer would get by asking backwards about a relationship that does hold.
failure_mode.owner: UNOWNED -- no seat is named as owning orientation discoverability for a consumer.

verdict.why: Direction is real, total, and structurally guaranteed: it is inherited from the Kuzu REL model rather than implemented per-edge, so there is no representable edge that lacks it, and a control pair from different truths confirms it is asymmetric in practice (280 forward, 0 reversed) rather than merely declared. D2 can stand on it, and provenance and blast-radius -- both of which need only direction and grain -- are computable today because of it. QUALIFIED rather than SOUND on three bounded defects: (1) the wrong orientation returns a clean zero indistinguishable from a true negative, which is the failure a consumer will actually meet; (2) all 53 edge types share one REL table, so a naturally symmetric relation is still stored asymmetrically and nothing tells a consumer which orientation is meaningful per type; (3) direction guarantees ORDER, never CORRECTNESS -- a backwards-written edge is perfectly directed and perfectly wrong, and this card measures the former only. Not UNSOUND: none of these makes direction unusable, and the first two are properties a consumer can work around once told. NOT INCOMPLETE: all 7 rows are worked. Two scalars sit below measured -- methodology at 'inferred' because I could not identify the projection's builder and so cannot claim its currency, and key at 'absent' because node-id stability across rebuilds needs two vintages and I had one. ⛔ NO FORWARD DISPOSITION per W2-m-3: omitted, and nothing here is an opinion on this subject's future. Per QUALIFY-DO-NOT-FIX this lane remediated nothing.
blocking_defects: For any consumer querying a directed edge: the wrong orientation returns 0, not an error. Check both directions before concluding two nodes are unrelated. Owner UNOWNED.
For any consumer treating direction as semantic correctness: it guarantees order only. A backwards edge is undetectable by this property. Owner UNOWNED.
For any consumer of a naturally symmetric edge type: it is still stored asymmetrically and the schema does not say which orientation is meaningful. Owner UNOWNED.
